mcqs.question: You train 100 identical decision trees on the exact same training data (no bootstrapping, no randomness) and average their predictions. What happens to the variance?
options: It stays essentially unchanged, since the trees' errors are perfectly correlated
It drops by roughly a factor of 100, as with any ensemble
It increases, because averaging always adds noise
It drops to exactly zero since averaging removes all error
mcqs.explanation: The variance-reduction formula (σ²/N) only holds when errors are independent. Identical trees on identical data make identical errors — perfectly correlated — so averaging them cancels nothing. This is exactly why bagging and random forest deliberately inject randomness before averaging.

mcqs.question: Why does random forest restrict each split to a random subset of features, on top of bagging's bootstrap sampling?
options: It's purely a speed optimization with no effect on accuracy
It prevents a few dominant features from making every tree's top splits nearly identical, further decorrelating the trees
It's required to compute Gini impurity correctly
It guarantees every tree reaches the same depth
mcqs.explanation: Bagging alone still lets one or two strong features dominate the top split of almost every tree, keeping the trees correlated. Restricting the feature subset per split forces different trees down different structural paths, which is the extra decorrelation random forest needs to outperform plain bagged trees. It's not primarily about speed, impurity computation, or depth.

mcqs.question: A random forest's Gini-based feature importance ranks a raw customer ID field above a genuinely predictive age feature. What's the most likely explanation?
options: Customer ID is a real causal driver of the target and should be kept
The random forest is broken and needs retraining with more trees
The high number of distinct values in customer ID gives it more chances to appear to reduce impurity, inflating its Gini importance
Age must be scaled before it can compete in importance rankings
mcqs.explanation: High-cardinality features get more candidate split points, which can make Gini importance look inflated even without real predictive power. This is a known bias of impurity-based importance, not a sign the model is broken, and it isn't fixed by feature scaling — permutation importance on held-out data is the more reliable comparison.
